title: Large seasonal Atlantic thermal rises and falls had no clear attenuation difference in NOAA fields for 2005-2025
abstract: We tested whether large local thermal sea-level rises and falls had different reductions in total steric change in NOAA upper-700-m fields for 2005-2025. We removed quarter means and linear trends, took seasonal increments, and selected changes above a local 90th percentile fitted outside each scored start year. Total changes were smaller in 75.21% of selected Atlantic rises and 75.04% of falls. The difference was 0.17 percentage points, with conditional 95% three-year block limits of -1.44 to +1.77 points. The rise-to-fall log contrast in total-to-thermal squared-change ratios was -0.0042 [-0.0899, 0.0973]. A local linear reference also gave no clear contrast. All planned Atlantic checks retained intervals that included zero. The primary Pacific and Indian contrasts were also uncertain. These null results do not prove equal physical responses. One mapped product, fixed fitted thresholds, a short record, and unequal event locations and sizes limit inference. The package gives original code, exact source paths and hashes, 750 basin-year-sign summary rows, resample scores, a figure, independent source checks, and instructions for reproduction. Raw source fields remain external.

display.caption: Large seasonal thermal rises and falls had uncertain differences. Lines show conditional 95% three-year block limits. The right panel subtracts the contrast predicted by a local linear reference.
